author: reek
body: A TLS 1.3 handshake completing WITHOUT authentication, and the same client refusing to complete when it asked for authentication and did not get it. Both halves matter and they are the same code path.

author: reek
body: A client with no trust anchors does not require the server to be authenticated. It still cannot verify the certificate, and until this test existed that was fatal for the wrong reason: the Certificate and CertificateVerify messages were folded into the transcript only when they verified, so a client that could not verify them held a transcript one message short of the server's and the server Finished never matched. The handshake failed at the Finished, which reads like a key schedule fault and is nothing of the kind.

author: reek
body: The transcript records what was RECEIVED. Authentication is a separate verdict carried by tep-auth-done, and tep-auth-missing is what refuses.

author: reek
body: no-anchors is the case that could not complete before. tampered is the control that proves the fix did not buy it by weakening anything: that client DOES carry the real anchor, so it requires authentication, and it is handed a Certificate with a flipped byte. It must not finish.

author: reek
body: One server, used by both clients. It presents the real leaf chain either way; what differs is what the client is willing to check.

author: reek
body: anchors is empty, so this client does not require authentication. It cannot verify the chain and does not try to; it must still complete, because completing is a property of the transcript and the key schedule, not of whether it liked the certificate.

author: reek
body: Application data proves the handshake produced usable keys on both sides, which a Finished check alone does not.

target: section:A Client That Asked For Authentication And Was Cheated
author: reek
body: This client carries the real anchor, so it requires authentication. The Certificate it receives has a flipped byte, so the chain does not walk, no peer key is kept, and the CertificateVerify cannot check out. Both messages still fold, so its transcript matches the server's and the server Finished verifies -- and it must STILL refuse, on the authentication verdict alone.
